event_type.format: One fixed word, case-sensitive; AwsApiCall on most records.
event_type.quote: Identifies the type of event that generated the event record.

AwsApiCall.meaning: An API was called: the ordinary record, one per request.

AwsServiceEvent.meaning: A service generated the event on its own, for instance when another account used a resource you own; no caller sent this request.

AwsConsoleAction.meaning: A person clicked around inside the web console itself; nothing here came in over the API.

AwsConsoleSignIn.meaning: A sign-in to the AWS Management Console by a root, IAM, federated, SAML or SwitchRole user.

AwsVpceEvents.meaning: A network activity event: an API call through a VPC endpoint, recorded only when the endpoint owner enables network activity events for that event source.

AwsCloudTrailInsight.meaning: A CloudTrail Insights record: an API call rate or error rate that left the baseline. Its record format is its own.
AwsCloudTrailInsight.note: Not on the record-contents page for management, data and network events; Insights records are documented separately.

examples.note: an ordinary API request; the bulk of any trail
a console sign-in; additionalEventData says whether MFA was used

identity_type.format: One fixed word, case-sensitive. Root, IAMUser and AssumedRole cover most records; SAMLUser and WebIdentityUser appear on the AWS STS federation calls.

Root.meaning: The account's root credentials. userName carries the account alias when one is set, and is absent otherwise.

IAMUser.meaning: An IAM user's own long-term credentials; userName is the user.

AssumedRole.meaning: Temporary credentials from AWS STS AssumeRole, including EC2 instance roles and cross-account access; the role is in sessionContext.sessionIssuer.

Role.meaning: A persistent IAM role identity; the session issuer is always the role itself.

FederatedUser.meaning: Temporary credentials from AWS STS GetFederationToken; sessionIssuer says whether root or an IAM user called it.

Directory.meaning: A request to a directory service (Amazon WorkDocs, Amazon Quick) whose identity type is not known.

AWSAccount.meaning: Another AWS account, typically one that assumed a role you own; you see it because the role is yours.

AWSService.meaning: An account belonging to an AWS service, acting on your behalf: Elastic Beanstalk assuming a role in your account, for instance.

IdentityCenterUser.meaning: A caller signed in through IAM Identity Center; onBehalfOf carries the user's id and identity store.
IdentityCenterUser.quote: A request made on behalf of an IAM Identity Center user; onBehalfOf names the user id and the identity store.

Unknown.meaning: CloudTrail could not determine the identity type.

SAMLUser.meaning: AWS STS AssumeRoleWithSAML: the request carried a SAML assertion; identityProvider names the IdP.

WebIdentityUser.meaning: AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity: a web identity provider (Cognito, Google, Login with Amazon, Facebook) vouched for the caller.

examples.note: temporary credentials from a role; the role itself is in sessionContext.sessionIssuer
a service acting in your account; userIdentity.invokedBy names it

error_code.format: Absent when the call succeeded. Otherwise the calling service's own error string, not a fixed set: AccessDenied and its kin from IAM, Client.<Name> and Server.<Name> from EC2, <Name>Exception from most other services. Truncated at 1 KB.
error_code.quote: The AWS service error if the request returns an error.

AccessDenied.meaning: IAM refused the call, explicitly (a Deny statement) or implicitly (no policy allowed it). errorMessage names the policy type, and sometimes the policy, when the service uses the newer message format.

VpceAccessDenied.meaning: A VPC endpoint policy refused the call; only on network activity events.

UnauthorizedOperation.meaning: EC2's authorization refusal. When the message is encoded, sts:DecodeAuthorizationMessage unpacks it.

Client.UnauthorizedOperation.meaning: The same EC2 refusal with the client-error prefix, which is how CloudTrail usually records it.

AuthFailure.meaning: EC2 could not validate the credentials: wrong keys, or an account not authorized for EC2.

Client.InvalidInstanceID.NotFound.meaning: EC2: no such instance, or one created so recently that its id has not propagated yet.

examples.note: a burst of these from one principal across services is enumeration
EC2's spelling of the same refusal

session_issuer_type.format: One fixed word, only inside sessionContext (temporary credentials): Role, IAMUser or Root.
session_issuer_type.quote: The source of the temporary security credentials, such as Root, IAMUser, or Role.

Role.meaning: The session came from assuming a role, whether an IAM user, a service or a web identity user assumed it; userName is the role name.

IAMUser.meaning: An IAM user's credentials issued the session (GetSessionToken, GetFederationToken); userName is that user's name.

Root.meaning: Root credentials issued the session; userName is the account alias when one is set.

examples.note: the usual case, an assumed role; sessionIssuer.userName is the role name

principal_id.format: AIDA-prefixed id for an IAM user, or AROA-prefixed role id plus a colon and session name for assumed roles.

examples.note: assumed role id plus session name

principal_arn.format: ARN of the caller; for an assumed role this is the session ARN, not the role's own ARN.

caller_account_id.format: 12-digit account id that owns the entity used to sign the request.

access_key_id.format: AKIA prefix marks a long-term IAM user key; ASIA prefix marks temporary STS credentials.

user_name.format: The IAM user's or root alias's friendly name string; masked or absent for role sessions.

invoked_by.format: A service principal name (service.amazonaws.com), present only when an AWS service made the request on the principal's behalf.

elasticbeanstalk.amazonaws.com.meaning: Elastic Beanstalk assuming a role in your account to call other services for you.

autoscaling.amazonaws.com.meaning: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling launching or terminating instances on your behalf.

ec2.amazonaws.com.meaning: Amazon EC2 itself, for instance an instance profile fetching its role credentials.

cloudformation.amazonaws.com.meaning: CloudFormation acting for the principal during a stack operation.

config.amazonaws.com.meaning: AWS Config evaluating or recording resources on your behalf.

AWS Internal.meaning: An AWS-originated request where the calling service is not named.

federated_provider.format: Provider name in sessionContext.webIdFederationData.federatedProvider for a role assumed via web identity.

identity_provider.format: External identity provider name in userIdentity.identityProvider, for SAMLUser or WebIdentityUser callers.

on_behalf_of_user_id.format: UUID-style identity-store user id in userIdentity.onBehalfOf.userId for an Identity Center caller.

user_identity.format: Nested JSON object holding type, principalId, arn, accountId, accessKeyId, userName and sessionContext.

cim_user.format: TA-derived caller or target username string, picked from a long eventName-keyed EVAL in props.conf.

examples.note: caller name, or target user for user-mgmt events

cim_user_arn.format: TA-derived ARN string: userIdentity.arn if present, else requestParameters.roleArn.

caller_name.format: TA-derived friendly name string: userName, else session issuer's name, else the ARN's last path segment.

cim_vendor_account.format: TA-derived 12-digit account id: userIdentity.accountId if present, else recipientAccountId.

account_of_record.format: TA-derived 12-digit account id: recipientAccountId for AWSAccount/AWSService callers, else userIdentity.accountId.

session_credential_from_console.format: String literal true, marking a call made via an AWS Management Console session; omitted when false.

true.meaning: Call originated from a console session; the client was a proxy or an external client.

session_issuer_arn.format: ARN of the role or user that issued the session, at sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn

session_issuer_user_name.format: Friendly name of the role or user that issued the session, at sessionIssuer.userName

session_issuer_principal_id.format: Unique principal ID of the issuing role or user, at sessionIssuer.principalId

session_issuer_account_id.format: Account ID that owns the issuing role or user, at sessionIssuer.accountId

session_mfa_authenticated.format: String flag at sessionContext.attributes.mfaAuthenticated showing whether the caller used MFA

true.meaning: Root or IAM user authenticated with an MFA device for this session

false.meaning: No MFA device was used to authenticate this session

session_creation_date.format: Timestamp the temporary credentials were issued, at sessionContext.attributes.creationDate, ISO 8601 basic notation

examples.note: ISO 8601 basic, no dashes or colons

ec2_role_delivery.format: Version string at sessionContext.ec2RoleDelivery naming which IMDS version delivered the role credentials

1.0.meaning: Credentials came from IMDSv1, the request/response scheme with no session token.

2.0.meaning: Credentials came from IMDSv2, the session-oriented scheme that requires a token.

issued_temp_key_id.format: Temporary access key ID issued with the session, always prefixed ASIA

issued_credential_expiration.format: When the issued temporary credentials expire; CloudTrail renders it as a human-readable date, not ISO 8601.

examples.note: as CloudTrail renders it in responseElements

assumed_role_session_id.format: Role's principal ID with the session name appended, returned as AssumedRoleUser.AssumedRoleId

examples.note: AssumedRoleId, principal ID plus session name

requested_role_arn.format: ARN of the role being assumed, passed as the AssumeRole RoleArn request parameter

role_session_name.format: Caller-chosen free-text identifier for the role session, logged and visible cross-account

created_access_key_id.format: New long-term IAM user access key ID from CreateAccessKey, always prefixed AKIA

event_version.format: Major.minor schema version of the record; minor bumps add fields, major bumps break structure

1.01.meaning: Adds requestID, eventID, apiVersion, readOnly, resources

1.02.meaning: Adds recipientAccountId and the eventType field

1.03.meaning: Adds sharedEventID for events delivered to multiple accounts

1.07.meaning: Adds eventCategory and the Insights event fields

1.11.meaning: Adds eventContext for enriched event data stores

event_time.format: Timestamp of when the request completed, UTC, in ISO 8601 format

event_source.format: DNS-style hostname the request went to, usually the service short name plus .amazonaws.com

monitoring.amazonaws.com.meaning: Amazon CloudWatch API, the naming convention's stated exception

event_name.format: The API action name called, in PascalCase matching the service's API reference

event_category.format: Enum grouping the record by which kind of event logging produced it

Management.meaning: Set on control-plane operations such as creating or configuring a resource

Data.meaning: Set on data events, item-level operations like S3 object or Lambda actions

NetworkActivity.meaning: Set on network activity events, recorded via a VPC endpoint only when enabled

event_id.format: Unique CloudTrail-assigned GUID for this single record

request_id.format: Request identifier the called service itself assigned and returned to the caller

shared_event_id.format: GUID shared by the paired records CloudTrail delivers to two different accounts for one action

management_event.format: Boolean shown from eventVersion 1.06 on, true for control-plane event types

true.meaning: A management event: AwsApiCall, AwsConsoleAction, AwsConsoleSignIn, or AwsServiceEvent

false.meaning: Not a management event (a data or network activity event)

read_only.format: Boolean marking whether the called operation only reads, without changing state

true.meaning: Reads state without changing it; DescribeTrails is one example

false.meaning: Can write or change state; DeleteTrail is one example

api_version.format: The service API's own version string, present only for services (like EC2) that version their API

recipient_account_id.format: The 12-digit account ID that received and recorded this event

aws_region.format: Region code the request was made to, for example us-east-2

request_parameters.format: Nested object of the call's input parameters; shape depends on eventName, capped at 100 KB

response_elements.format: Nested object of what the call returned; null for read-only or failed calls, capped at 100 KB

additional_event_data.format: Extra service-specific data outside the request/response, for example MFAUsed on a console sign-in

service_event_details.format: For AwsServiceEvent records, what the service did on its own, for example a KMS key rotation

cim_object_category.format: The TA's aws_cloudtrail_eventname_lookup maps eventName to an object type such as instance or user

cim_change_type.format: The TA's lookup maps eventName/eventSource to a CIM Change type such as AAA or network

AAA.meaning: Authentication, authorization, or accounting activity (sign-in, assume-role)

network.meaning: Networking resource change (VPC, security group, route)

vpc_endpoint_id.format: VPC endpoint id string identifying the endpoint requests traversed; typically vpce- prefix plus a hex suffix

source_ip.format: Dotted IPv4 or IPv6 address the request came from; an AWS service's DNS name replaces it for AWS-originated calls
source_ip.quote: For services in AWS, only the DNS name is displayed

examples.note: AWS service acting on your behalf

user_agent.format: Free-text client identifier string sent with the request; format varies by SDK, CLI build, or calling service

tls_version.format: TLS protocol version string the client negotiated with the service endpoint

TLSv1.2.meaning: TLS 1.2 was negotiated: older SDKs and CLIs, and the oldest version AWS endpoints still accept.

TLSv1.3.meaning: TLS 1.3 was negotiated: current SDKs, CLIs and the console.

tls_cipher_suite.format: Cipher suite name string the client and service agreed on for the TLS session

tls_client_host_header.format: Host header value the client sent, usually the FQDN of the service endpoint it addressed

tls_details.format: Nested object with tlsVersion, cipherSuite and clientProvidedHostHeader for the TLS connection used

target_user_name.format: IAM user name string identifying the user an operation acts on, not the caller

policy_arn.format: Full ARN string of the IAM managed policy referenced by the operation

bucket_name.format: S3 bucket name string carried in requestParameters.bucketName for the operation

object_key.format: S3 object key path string carried in requestParameters.key on data-event operations

instance_type.format: EC2 instance type string requested for the new instance

requested_instance_id.format: EC2 instance id string(s) the operation targets, from requestParameters.instancesSet.items

security_group_id.format: Security group id string, sg- prefix plus a hex suffix, identifying the group changed

cidr_ip.format: IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR block string being authorized or revoked on the rule

examples.note: open to all IPv4, classic finding

launched_instance_id.format: EC2 instance id string(s) assigned to instances RunInstances created, in responseElements

created_user_name.format: IAM user name string of the user CreateUser just created, from responseElements.user.userName

resource_arn.format: Full ARN string of a resource the operation touched, listed under resources[].ARN

resource_type.format: Resource type identifier string in the form AWS::service::data-type, one per resources[] entry

AWS::IAM::Role.meaning: An IAM role was the resource touched by the call

AWS::IAM::SAMLProvider.meaning: A SAML identity provider resource was touched

AWS::KMS::Key.meaning: A KMS key was the resource for a key management call

AWS::S3::Bucket.meaning: An S3 bucket was the resource touched by the call

AWS::IAM::User.meaning: An IAM user was the resource touched by the call

resource_account_id.format: 12-digit account id string of a resource's owner, listed under resources[].accountId

image_id.format: TA aliases requestParameters.instancesSet.items{}.imageId onto image_id via a FIELDALIAS in props.conf

rule_action.format: TA derives allow/deny for network ACL rule changes via an EVAL in props.conf on the raw action code

allow.meaning: TA-derived: the ACL rule permits the matched traffic

deny.meaning: TA-derived: the ACL rule blocks the matched traffic

error_message.format: A free text sentence explaining the failure, sometimes naming the denied principal, action, and missing permission.

examples.value: User: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/John is not authorized to perform: codecommit:ListRepositories because no identity-based policy allows the codecommit:ListRepositories action

insight_details.format: Nested object: state (Start or End), eventSource, eventName, insightType, and insightContext with baseline and insight call rate stats.

cim_action.format: TA looks up eventName plus errorCode in aws-cloudtrail-action-status-lookup and returns a CIM action verb, or failure on error.

created.meaning: Successful call that created a resource.

deleted.meaning: Successful call that deleted a resource.

modified.meaning: Successful call that changed a resource's configuration.

read.meaning: Successful call that only read data.

updated.meaning: Successful call that updated a resource's state or content.

failure.meaning: The lookup found an errorCode on the event.

cim_status.format: TA looks up eventName plus errorCode in the same action-status lookup table and returns success or failure.

success.meaning: The API call completed without an errorCode.

failure.meaning: The API call returned an errorCode.

outcome_message.format: TA coalesces errorCode with the literal 'success' when no errorCode is present on the event.

success.meaning: No errorCode was present on the event.

AccessDeniedException.meaning: The event's errorCode, copied through unchanged.

UnauthorizedOperation.meaning: The event's errorCode, copied through unchanged.

AuthFailure.meaning: The event's errorCode, copied through unchanged.

result_message.format: TA derived text: the event's errorMessage if present, otherwise a per-eventName response element string.

console_login_result.format: Literal Success or Failure copied from the ConsoleLogin event's responseElements.ConsoleLogin field.

Success.meaning: The console sign in attempt succeeded.

Failure.meaning: The console sign in attempt failed.

console_mfa_used.format: Literal Yes or No from additionalEventData.MFAUsed on the ConsoleLogin or GetSigninToken event.

Yes.meaning: The root or IAM user signed in using multi factor authentication.

No.meaning: The user signed in without multi factor authentication.

console_login_to.format: The full console URL string from additionalEventData.LoginTo, the page the user landed on after signing in.

examples.note: landed on the console home page

authentication_method.format: TA combines additionalEventData.MFAUsed with the session's mfaAuthenticated attribute into MFA or SFA.

MFA.meaning: MFAUsed is Yes, or the session's mfaAuthenticated attribute is true.

SFA.meaning: Neither MFA signal is true, single factor authentication.

provenance.statement: A column of the AWS S3 connector's table; the reference lists AwsApiCall, AwsServiceEvent, AwsConsoleAction and AwsConsoleSignIn.
A column of the AWS S3 connector's table; the reference lists Root, IAMUser, AssumedRole, FederatedUser, Directory, AWSAccount, AWSService and Unknown.
Splunk Add-on for AWS, props.conf [aws:cloudtrail]: FIELDALIAS eventType AS app
Splunk Add-on for AWS, props.conf [aws:cloudtrail]: FIELDALIAS errorCode AS result_id
